day_shape: 85 items: IRGC claims strike on US radar in Bahrain (CENTCOM says two drones downed, no damage), Iran reports tanker mine-strike and four tanker explosions in Strait of Hormuz, IAEA flags uninspected Isfahan enrichment plant, OFAC publishes Iran GLs W/EE/FF, and heavy Khamenei Fatimiyya mourning cycle.

threads.label: Bahrain radar claim and CENTCOM rebuttal
threads.summary: Iranian state media and the IRGC said they struck a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, the first such claim on US Gulf assets since September. CENTCOM said two one-way attack drones were launched and both shot down with no injuries or damage, a position echoed by Iran International.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker incidents
threads.summary: Iran's military said four oil tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings, and the IRGC Navy reported an LNG tanker struck a naval mine on an "unauthorised" route. Ex-Mossad chief David Barnea argued a Hormuz blockade is the best option to stop Iran's nuclear programme.

threads.label: IAEA concerns and nuclear doctrine debate
threads.summary: A report seen by Reuters said the IAEA is "increasingly concerned" about an underground Isfahan enrichment plant declared over a year ago but never inspected. Iran International reported the Assembly of Experts has called for a review of Iran's defence doctrine, potentially reopening the religious ban on nuclear weapons.

threads.label: US sanctions and diplomatic posture
threads.summary: OFAC published Iran-related General Licenses W, EE and FF, alongside a White House presidential determination under NDAA FY2012 section 1245(d). Trump told Salem News Channel he could renew strikes on Iran, directed VP Vance away from Iran talks, and said no deal was needed as the regime was "collapsing".

threads.label: Yemen sanctions renewed at UNSC
threads.summary: The Security Council adopted Resolution 2837 (2026) renewing Yemen targeted sanctions for 12 months and extending the Panel of Experts mandate for 13. The UK's Ambassador MacIntosh delivered an explanation of vote, as Saudi Arabia pressed the EU to designate the Houthis and Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure at Yanbu and Riyadh.

threads.label: Gaza humanitarian and Nasser Hospital strike
threads.summary: The IDF said 93,000+ tents and 8,600+ winter-supply trucks have entered Gaza since preparations began, and that a strike at Nasser Hospital targeted Khan Younis Brigade commander Muhammad Abu Ismail. UK Minister Doughty addressed the Commons on Gaza and MacIntosh delivered a multi-state Call to Action on humanitarian access; Defa Press claimed a nine-month-old died of hypothermia.

threads.label: Khamenei Fatimiyya mourning cycle and IRGC messaging
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted a stream of audio and video from the Zeinabiyyah mourning ceremony for Fatima al-Zahra, and announced a headquarters to commemorate the "Bloody Ascension of the Mujahid Imam Martyr". IRIB carried the IRGC chief and Tehran Friday Prayer Leader warning of "terrible and painful" responses, alongside an Army claim it downed an MQ-1 drone near Sirik.

events.title: Iran's top clerical governing body calls for nuclear doctrine review
events.summary: Iran's Assembly of Experts, a body of Islamic jurists tasked with choosing the supreme leader, has become the first governing institution to call for a review of the country's defense doctrine, potentially paving the way for a reversal of the religious ban on nuclear weapons.

events.title: Notice of OFAC Sanctions Action
events.summary: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is publishing the names of one or more persons that have been placed on OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List) based on OFAC's determination that one or more applicable legal criteria were satisfied. All property and interests in property subject to U.S. jurisdiction of these persons are blocked, and U.S. persons are generally prohibited from engaging in transactions with them.

details.agencies: Treasury Department, Foreign Assets Control Office
